name: K10 - San Diego
_ui_series_doc: Engine track_folder prefixes the CM display name with ui_series (default 'K10 Colorado'); empty = use the track name as-is (SD names already carry the K10 - San Diego branding).
author: k10-san-diego
_about: A single drivable LOOP around Lake Murray (Kevin's childhood neighborhood). This repo is the standalone, Blender-first home for the track: the loop is mapped from the REAL roads (OpenStreetMap) at REAL elevation (USGS 3DEP), imported into Blender, and shaped there interactively (Kevin designs, Claude operates) BEFORE any kn5 export. Start point = just the 5-road main loop; everything else is added deliberately, in Blender.

source._doc: The loop is stitched from the named roads below along the real OSM drivable network (route.stitch='network'), then sampled for real elevation. data/network.cache.json is a cached OSM fetch so re-derivation never depends on a live Overpass call.

route._bbox_doc: Ledger 0054 P0 step 5 (2026-10-14): grown from [32.76, -117.075, 32.808, -116.998] to take the north loop (Waring, Princess View, Mission Gorge, Jackson north: J3 at -117.0790, J4 at 32.8171 N; EXPANSION-PLAN 'at least N 32.820 / W -117.082'). South and east unchanged. Read only by the centreline stage (scripts-v021/gps/centerline.py) and the buildings/zones fetchers' default box; no SD ship step reads it. The expansion's own OSM snapshot is data/osm.expansion.json (bbox 32.755 / -117.115 / 32.850 / -116.985, tools/fetch_osm.py, 7-day guard).
route._split_carriageways_doc: DELETED 2026-08-19 (campaign C1; ledger 0029 decision, closes 0032+0035). The split-carriageway machinery produced the College Ave sawtooth (286 mainline verts clamped to 9 m in 35 disjoint stripes) and the phantom floating _opp ribbons (college_avenue_opp 1585 m, navajo_road_opp) that connected to nothing. Do not re-add without a junction model.
route._divided_connectors_doc: Ledger 0039 (Kevin's seat, 2026-10-08: side streets 'not connecting correctly'). Del Cerro Boulevard is a divided boulevard whose two carriageways OSM stores as one out-and-back loop (the connector polyline parallels itself at 12-15 m for 0-475 / 625-1100); tools/divide_connectors.py collapses the legs into one trunk ribbon + median island (far loop kept as a plain ribbon) so it meets College as ONE mouth with a set-back nose.
route._median_islands_doc: Ledger 0037 (Kevin's seat, 2026-08-20): C1's single slab 'loses realism because that road doesn't look like that there' — the real streets are divided by raised landscaped medians ('flowers and barriers... grass etc... shrubs'). The rt_macau pattern (docs/JUNCTIONS.md): ONE continuous pavement slab, median standing ON it as a raised island. tools/median_envelope.py measures the real median from the OSM dual-carriageway geometry, re-centers the ribbon over the true middle and spans both carriageways; tools/author_median_blend.py authors the island (grass deck, shrub clumps, barrier runs) after build_loop_blend, gapped at every connector mouth.
route._median_registration_doc: Ledger 0055 round 2 (the truth lens: College's lanes sat east of the real road). Raw-centreline vertices (centerline.raw.local.json.pre-median) and the lateral move of the FINISHED divided road, metres, + = left of the vertex order (west on College northbound), cosine between points (tools/median_envelope.registration). MEASURED 2026-10-14 in the engine frame (WGS84 series) on two independent sources that agree within ~0.5-1 m: USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar cross-sections every 4 verts over v1190-1430 (the median slope's half-height point between the southbound and the 2-6 m higher northbound bench) and NAIP 2022-04-25 (m_3211716_sw_11_060) read on the ImageServer's SERVED extent (it widens the latitude extent to square-degree pixels; reading a tile on its requested bbox squeezes it ~16 % north-south, which put every earlier aerial check 3-12 m off). Model island centre minus the real median middle, smoothed +-10 verts: 2.0 (v1190), 2.6 (1220), 3.4 (1250), 4.3 (1280-1300), 4.7 (1310-1330), 5.5 (1350-1370), 4.3 (1400), 3.75 (1430), NAIP 4.55 (1485) / 3.2 (1495). Cause: OSM draws both College ways 2-4 m east of their pavement, and median_envelope's sphere projection of OSM adds 1.3-2.1 m (its trusted() doc). Ramps: in from the Del Cerro Blvd mouth's island gap (ends v1100) over 1104-1190, out over 1485-1505 inside the run's own taper into the Navajo box (1506). Height is untouched (the deck keeps the southbound grade, Kevin's 0055 choice).

route_connectors._authored_routes_doc: Ledger 0054 P0 step 5 (2026-10-14; Kevin 2026-10-12: 'the new loop will connect to the old one'). north = airoso data/routes.json 'north' (tools/route_append.py from data/route.north.spec.json on data/osm.expansion.json): J1 (College/Waring) -> Waring -> Princess View -> Mission Gorge -> Jackson north -> J5 (Navajo/Jackson), both directions, one-way tags respected. Its roads are 17-33 m divided boulevards, so route_connectors does NOT draw it as constant connector_width_m pieces (EXPANSION-PLAN A3): an authored route is HELD (listed, no connector drawn) until P1 writes the readable intermediate (data/expansion.north.json, tools/author_expansion.py) and P3 has route_connectors take it over. Held = the connectors this tool writes are byte-identical to the [medium, short] set (tests/tools/test_route_connectors_held.py).
route_connectors._doc: Ledger 0041 (Kevin's seat, 2026-10-08): side streets disjointed. The per-name connectors missed Madra Ave and Delaware Ave and never had Pennsylvania Lane; tools/route_connectors.py derives the side streets from airoso data/routes.json (tools/route_tracks.py — Kevin's confirmed routes as continuous OSM node paths): the medium/short routes' off-loop runs become connector pieces, cut at College / the Del Cerro trunk by trim_connectors. route.connectors above is now documentation of the old name-based set.
route_connectors._authored_take_doc: Ledger 0054 P3 step 1 (2026-10-18): the north route is no longer HELD. tools/route_connectors.py takes the intermediate's four road PIECES whole (A Waring, B Princess View, C Mission Gorge, D Jackson north; tools/expansion_pieces.py): the pavement midline + curb-to-curb width per station (A3), A and D starting with P1's weld stubs W1 / W5 (so D runs J5 -> J4), B / C and the far ends of A / D ending exactly on the J2 / J3 / J4 pad arm cuts; the 3DEP profile through a local quadratic fit (the 11 % cap binds nowhere). P1's rehearsal took only the two weld stubs ([W1, W5]).

route._tight_approach_doc: Ledger 0054 P3 (2026-10-18; tools/seat_terrain_blend.py, opt-in): a side street whose mouth's host climbs at least 6 % [invented] has its whole approach's ground halved to 0.75 m (the seat's TIGHT_EDGE_M, as under a tight corner): the weld eases a 9 % host cross-fall to level over a 15 m stub's every row, and a 1.5 m grass facet across that twist stood 1-4 mm under the stub's road (verify_mouths APPROACH at Fontaine St / Princess View Way, P3's second build).
route._junction_pads_doc: Ledger 0054 P3 step 2 (2026-10-18; EXPANSION-PLAN A4, docs/JUNCTIONS.md topology B): the three new crossroads J2 / J3 / J4 as one junction pad each (tools/junction_pad.py plan + tools/author_junction_pad_blend.py; gate tools/verify_pads.py): the deck welded onto every route arm's last row (seams 0.000 m), true-arc corners at the measured curb-return radii every 0.75 m, the curb + walk round every corner, and every unbuilt arm a Phase 5 closed stub (JUNCTIONS 18(d)): 15 m of real road to Kevin's K-rail, its far edge at 3DEP (data/pads.3dep.json).
route._north_welds_doc: Ledger 0054 P3 step 3 (2026-10-18): P1's rehearsal delta (source/expansion/p1-proofs/rehearsal_delta.py, P1 fix round) made permanent: aprons {AP1} = J1's R 30 return (tools/author_aprons_blend.py); trim_blend_grade_cap [north_] = the welded pieces' blends onto the loop deck lengthened until they stay within the 11 % cap (Waring fell 14.8 % in 30 m: the loop stands 1.44 m over 3DEP at J1); mouth_fill [north_] = their strips over the loop's pavement replaced by one piece from the loop's own edge; weld_exact_deck [north_] = the weld reads the loop deck off its triangles (the J1 corner's fanned outer edge). Each key names connector-name prefixes: only the two north mouths (J1, J5) carry them (the phase-5 stubs are STUB_*), but for weld_exact_deck, which also names STUB_: the north network's side streets join hosts that climb up to 9.6 % round curves (Princess View), where the level-across host deck read 2-3 cm off the host's own triangles at the mouth (verify_mouths HOST LANE, Laura St, P3's first build); the weld, the seat's host-lane refinement and verify_mouths then read the host deck off its triangles there, as at J1 / J5.
route._smooth_sigma_y_doc: Kevin 2026-10-09: 'smooth out the roughness'. The road profile is 3DEP sampled every 3 m (noise ~±10 cm) and build_loop_blend's vertical smoothing was sigma 1.5 pts (~4.5 m) — every sample step is a felt event (fleet/reference/MEASURED.md). 5.0 pts (~15 m) rounds the sample noise while keeping the real grades (climbs are hundreds of metres long). Measured by drive_test bumps/km + kinks/km vs the locked build.

_texture_overrides_doc: Engine-pbr parity: the engine's 1GRASS default is dry chaparral (Colorado tracks); Lake Murray's neighborhood terrain is irrigated green turf. Paths resolve against the engine checkout's assets/textures/ (pbr.load_overrides).

GRASS_FAR._doc: Ledger 0046 fix round (visual verify, 2026-10-12): the far ring wore pbr's stock ground_dry tile, a neutral grey gravel (mean RGB 139/132/122) - Cowles read as bare rock beside the green turf. This is grey-olive sage scrub over tan soil (mean 93/93/66), derived from the owned grass + ground_dry tiles (tracks/san-diego-lake-murray/textures/README.md); project-relative, synced into the workshop by tools/ship_sd.sh (TRACK_TEXTURES).

pbr._doc: network_walls: the merged freeway's 1WALL_fw barriers read as cast concrete (the network look), not Kevin's 4 m portable barrier modules. The loop itself has no plain 1WALL_ meshes (its rail is 1WALL_guard -> 1WALL_GUARD entry), so this only affects the combined build.

_layout_names_doc: Kevin 2026-10-12: "this will be called lake murray free roam vs the lake murray speedways (clockwise is normal, counterclockwise is reverse)" and "we may add mission gorge speedway etc". Scheme: <Area> Free Roam = the open network; <Area> Speedway = a race layout, clockwise the normal direction, anticlockwise <Area> Speedway Reverse. Layout ids (street / race_cw / race_acw) are folder names and stay, so saved setups and lap records survive.

layouts.name: Lake Murray Free Roam
layouts.run: open two-way street; lap clockwise: Alvarado westbound, College northbound, Navajo eastbound, Jackson south, Lake Murray Blvd southwest
layouts.ui_description: Lake Murray Free Roam — Lake Murray as it is: the open two-way 13.5 km loop of Alvarado Road, College Avenue, Navajo Road, Jackson Drive and Lake Murray Boulevard around the reservoir (Kevin's childhood neighbourhood), from OpenStreetMap at real USGS 3DEP elevation. Raised landscaped medians on College and Navajo, the side streets left open, no race furniture; lap clockwise from the line on Alvarado. The AI line is a generated draft, not an in-game recording.
layouts._doc: Version 1 = today's loop: main kn5 only, open mouths, full width, no race furniture. Only its spawn moves (ledger 0047 Q3): grid A on Alvarado, line v300. start_positions.json `active` still moves START/HOTLAP/PIT for THIS layout only (Kevin 2026-08-20 per-issue spawns) via tools/layout_dummies.py --issue-spawn, never AC_TIME, never the race layouts.

layouts.name: Lake Murray Speedway
layouts.run: clockwise, one-way: Alvarado westbound, College northbound, Navajo eastbound, Jackson south, Lake Murray Blvd southwest — your own side of every road (an Alvarado-wide lane), the whole street on Alvarado and the I-8 bridge, the full intersection open at the five corners

race._doc: Ledger 0049 (Kevin 2026-10-11: "racetrack versions of these, we need full intersections available for turning. And the entire other lane blocked off from access." / "more or less an Alvarado's width for the entire track with deviances in various areas" / open boxes at the "Corners the race turns at", side streets sealed). Replaces 0047's shared centre chain: each race layout gets its OWN corridor — the curb strip on its race side plus one closure wall (the same K-rail strip) standing so the lane is race.corridor.clear_width_m wide, along the race-side curb of each median island instead of on it, pinned into the far curb strip at every box edge; the whole street on Alvarado and the I-8 deck (corridor.whole); the full intersection open in each corridor.boxes; both curb strips one closed loop per side, across all three bridge spans (edge_gaps none). Read by tools/barrier_bands.py (version 2: the corridor solve + self-gates + planned no_route; FAILS if centre_runs is present or closure_runs differ from the derived ones), tools/race_corridor.py (the closure line), tools/author_race_furniture_blend.py, tools/layout_dummies.py and scripts/ac/write_ai_line.py (the race AI lane = corridors.<id>.lane_by_vertex). Each race layout loads ONLY its own <slug>_closure_<id>.kn5 (layouts[].closure_token names its meshes): the clockwise closure stands in the anticlockwise lane. Constants marked INVENTED in fleet/GATES-CHANGELOG.md; clear_width_m 11.36 is MEASURED (Alvarado 13.00 m - 2 x 0.82 as raced).

corridor._doc: Spec §9.1 (scratchpad corridor/spec.md, ledger 0049). whole = I-8 deck -> v0 -> Alvarado -> hairpin box (v4454 .. v777); boxes = the place_signs corner PC-2..PT+2 at the three interior corners (the seam and hairpin lie inside whole); closure_runs PINNED (College, Navajo, Jackson, Lake Murray Blvd); rates are 1:x lateral per metre of travel. clear_width_source alvarado = re-measured median(w - 2 x 0.82) over v25-723, fails beyond 0.02 m of clear_width_m. Tune only after Kevin's drive (spec §17).
corridor._boxes_apex_doc: Ledger 0055 round 2: the Jackson / Lake Murray Blvd apex reads v3296 (was v3297). The corner is unchanged (every centreline vertex from v1510 on is byte-identical); College's registration shortens the lap 0.45 m, which shifts place_signs' 1 m detector stations downstream and moves the max-curvature station from v3297 to v3296, 2.1 m apart on the R 10.8 m arc. barrier_bands self-gate 1 requires the declared apex to BE a detected one; the box v3289-3304 still holds PC v3291 .. PT v3302.

race._swept_mouths_doc: Ledger 0054 P3 step 6 (2026-10-18; P1's rehearsal delta made permanent): the two north mouths are declared where their swept edges open the loop edge, policy per vertex (A7): race_cw seals J1 with the far strip to the box pin v1521 and puts the rest behind its closure, race_acw with its race strip; J5 sealed_far_strip / sealed_race_strip.

kerbs._trims_doc: Ledger 0049 fix round (2026-10-11): hand-authored pull-backs of the detector's kerb runs, each measured on the scratch rehearsal's BUILT road kn5 (every 1ROAD sheet under the kerb's footprint at its lip, mid-line and outer edge, every 0.3 m station). A kerb laid across a ribbon fold (two road sheets, 0033/0046 class) sits UNDER the upper sheet: invisible from the seat, and audit K counts it against the lower sheet. drop = no single-sheet stretch of useful length reaches the apex; i / j = a pull-back to the stations where the road is one sheet. The folds themselves stay a named ribbon defect (the ribbon's owner). Read by tools/barrier_bands.py (kerbs / kerbs_dropped); verify_race E fails any authored kerb under another road sheet.

trims.why: Hairpin inside kerb (installed since 0047 at v751-775): 13 of its 139 stations sat under the other sheet of the hairpin's ribbon fold - v764 by up to 0.04 m, v774 by up to 0.14 m (the installed race_authored.json lists 0.166 m of other deck above it at v774). v751-763 is one sheet throughout: 111 stations, a 26 m kerb on the entry that stops 4 m short of the old trimmed corner; the 4 m exit leg (v774-775) goes.

College/Navajo inside apex: only 18 of the kerb's 34 stations sit on one sheet - about 1.5 m at each end (v1508-1509, v1518-1519); at v1517-1518 13 stations sit under the fold's upper sheet (up to 0.05 m) and 4 verts stand +0.13 m over the lower one (race audit K 158 vs the installed 154). No single-sheet stretch of useful length reaches the apex: dropped until the ribbon fold is one sheet.

Navajo/Jackson inside apex (race_cw's AI line apexes 1.5 m off it): the ribbon folds into two sheets up to 0.46 m apart at v2315 and v2323-2324, and 8 of the kerb's 51 stations sit under the upper sheet by up to 0.42 m - a red/white kerb vanishing under the asphalt at the apex. The single-sheet pieces are 4.5 m on entry (v2313-2314) and about 5 m on exit (v2324-2326), neither at the apex: dropped until the ribbon fold is one sheet.

Ledger 0054 A7: the J1 Waring opening (W1, v1514-v1526 on the outer curb) takes the whole outside of the College/Navajo corner the kerb ran along (v1507-1520); a kerb that ends at a road opening reads wrong. The inside kerb stays dropped for its own reason (above).
Ledger 0054 A7: the J5 Jackson-north opening (W5, v2312-v2322) covers the outside apex of the Navajo/Jackson corner (the kerb ran v2312-2327); only a 14 m exit stub would be left.

chicanes.name: college_split
chicanes.why: Ledger 0055 (Kevin, seat, 2026-10-14: 'for the racetrack versions, I do like the chicane that kind of goes from one side of the road across to the other and back'). v0.18.0's crossing was the ROAD jogging ~12 m sideways off the northbound carriageway onto the southbound one and back (tools/median_envelope.py's trust test, reading OSM through its own sphere projection, split College's divided run at v1280-1352); with the road where it really runs, the Speedways keep the crossing as race geometry on it (scripts/geometry/race_chicane.py, tools/barrier_bands.py: the closure sweeps into the far curb strip while a race-side wall sweeps in parallel from the race-side strip, ~108 m legs (36 vertices) centred on the v0.18.0 jogs (v1262-1280 / v1352-1370): 26 vertices stood at 1:2.85-3.0 against race.corridor.steepest_pin_rate 1:3, and 30 with race_chicane.EASE 0.2 bunched the AI line's turn-in under verify_ai_line's car scale; at 36 / EASE 0.35 the walls run 1:3.2-3.5, the lane held ~160 m on the far carriageway between the legs). Each Speedway crosses in its own direction: Speedway (race_cw, northbound) over to the southbound carriageway and back, Speedway Reverse (race_acw) the mirror. The median island from v1253 to v1379 stands in Lake Murray Free Roam only (<slug>_street.kn5): a race layout's road there is the bare slab the island stands on.

streetlight._doc: Kevin 2026-10-10: 'Can we do something about the lights? They're very harsh and very bright. And they need to be more like sodium lights from the 80s.' LOW-pressure sodium, not HPS: north of I-8 every City of San Diego street light was LPS from the Feb 1984 council vote (Palomar) until the 2002 broad-spectrum resolution, so Del Cerro's 80s lamps are the monochrome 589 nm yellow - color 255,165,30 (config is 0..1 floats, the writer scales x255) with single_frequency 0.9 as the sodium switch; HPS alternative if the hue reads wrong: color [1.0, 0.72, 0.30], single_frequency 0.7. 'Very bright' was a 255x scale error, not taste: CSP multiplies the 0..255 COLOR by intensity with no /255, so 1.6 was an effective 408 against a community median of ~10 (SRP 1.5); 0.01 = effective 2.55, the soft-sodium band. Ladder if too dark: 0.015 -> 0.02, ceiling 0.03, never back toward 0.1+. Harshness levers: SPOT 150 puts the cone rim (25.9 m at the 6.93 m light height) just outside the 24 m range edge so the gradient, not the cone, draws the pool; specular 0.6 -> 0.1 kills the asphalt glare; diffuse_concentration 0.25 + half-res blurred shadows soften the terminator and the black wedge under each post. emissive/emissive_color are inert here (LIGHTS_0_mat is the invisible 2 cm marker from the 2026-10-08 'glowing ball' fix, 5.0 -> 1.6 / 0.35 -> 0.08) but hue-matched for a future visible lens. Kevin 2026-10-11 after driving it: 'Lights need to be a bit brighter but not much' -> 0.010 -> 0.013 (+30%, under the planned 0.015 step); colour, cone and softness unchanged. Ledger 0056 (2026-10-14, the taller LED lamp: light 6.71 -> 11.43 m over the centreline, tools/streetlight_pool.py on CSP's documented range/spot/diffuse terms): UNDER each lamp the road stays in the RANGE_GRADIENT_OFFSET plateau (slant 11.4 m < 12.5 m) and the spot's full-strength core, so the brightness there is unchanged (+0.4 %); BETWEEN lamps the mid-block stays dark as before (3 % of midpoints lit, both) -> intensity stays 0.013, no scaling needed. What does change: the higher source puts the road 8-14 m from a lamp deeper in the cone, so the pool flanks are +16 % (quadratic fade) to +48 % (linear fade) brighter and the lit road +45-69 % on average, while the range sphere's ground footprint shrinks 24.0 -> ~22 m. If Kevin's seat reads that as brighter: 0.009 matches the road average (quadratic), 0.0077 (linear) - at the cost of the core under each lamp (-30-40 %); range_m 26.7 restores the 24 m footprint. 2026-10-14 (ledger 0056): with the taller LED lamps Kevin saw the preview and said 'They could be a little brighter' -> intensity 0.013 -> 0.015 (+15 %, the ladder's next step); seat-tune from here.

light_pollution._doc: Sky glow must match the lamps or the horizon reads as a different city. The writer default 1.0, 0.86, 0.66 is a warm-white LED-era sky; nohesi (Southern California freeway) ships 1.0, 0.7176, 0.2980 and la_canyons 255,183,76. density 0.22 / radius_km 6 / relative_position left at the writer defaults.

grassfx._doc: Kevin 2026-10-10 'add grassfx'. v1 = ONE look, weekly-mown irrigated suburban turf on both terrain tiles (parkway strips, median decks, front yards, Kiowa Dr park lawn), because CSP blades take the colour of the ground texel and the 1GRASS texture_override IS irrigated turf (mean sRGB 68,92,40). Right within ~10 m of the kerb and in the park; wrong on the reservoir slopes (annual oats/brome, gold straw late March to first rains = 8-9 months) in exactly the way the ground texture is already wrong - v1 adds no new lie and fixes none. Every key below is CSP grammar as shipped (ks_nordschleife own override, la_canyons A, vhr_phoenix, fn_bahrain); the writer's old [GRASS_FX_TEXTURE_0]/CONFIGURATION_0/BRIGHTNESS/HEALTH/grass_ks.dds grammar matched none of 90+ configs and is retired (a build now fails loud if those keys are set). mask 'open' = wiki spawn-everywhere preset -1/0/-1/1, chosen so blades certainly appear on first load (the MASK_MAIN formula is undocumented; both tiles are 100% grass so nothing is lost). shape_size 0.7-1.1: 0.7 is the fn_bahrain/vhr_phoenix dry-lawn floor (smaller = denser = costlier), 1.1 stays under the 1.2 cap so TreeFX median bushes (Bush 0.24-0.40) are not swallowed (la_canyons 'existing bushes'). shape_width 0.6 sits between dry 0.5 (Siracusa/thunderhill) and CSP's lush 1.0. tidy/cut 1->0.6/0.5 + TRIM_PERIOD THURSDAY = the mown idiom (Nords-own, la_canyons A, fn_bahrain). texture/texture_grid are the CSP-embedded highlands atlas, stated so the first drive also verifies the atlas v2 will use. LADDERS (config-only, regen + copy ini): too sparse/thin -> shape_size [0.6, 1.0]; too tall/dense -> [0.8, 1.1]; too uniform (golf course) -> add texture_groups [[{"piece": [4,1,2,2], "size_mult": [1.2,1.5], "wind": 0.5}]] + configurations {"A": {"texture_base_chance": 0.8, "texture_group_chances": [0.04]}} + adjustments [{"materials": ["1GRASS_0_mat","1GRASS_1_mat"], "map": "A"}]; patchier -> mask 'default' (colour-gated colorado-2013 quartet) with mask_blur 1; neon under the sodium lamps at night -> texture_brightness 0.8 (static, darkens day too); off without losing the tuning -> enabled false. NOT this key: the dry straw slopes need a straw ground texture under the blades = loop.blend split + kn5 rebuild (see fleet/feedback/0045 deferred list D1).

terrain._doc: Ledger 0046 (Kevin 2026-10-10: 'more terrain near the roads, and the I-8 trench and adjacent causeway cut out'; 'I want to see cowles mountain at least and maybe more of the i8 corridor when I'm up on Navajo'). fleet/LAWS.md L3 as amended 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-13 (ledger 0054 D3): near-road relief is shaped to the road within the road's own construction zone, ~20-40 m; real relief beyond is never reshaped (clamp_corridor_m 20 / clamp_blend_m 40, _clamp_doc). The ground is ONE multi-resolution lattice sampled from USGS 3DEP AT every vertex (scripts/elevation/terrain_sample.py, cached in data/terrain.samples.json.gz), anchored on the 20 m grid the assembler grades (tier_options.frame): 5 m cells (split in four) within 60 m of a pavement, 20 m (split in four) to 500 m, 40 m beyond, the I-8 corridor at 5 m and Cowles' cone at 20 m, over the dossier's landmark box (far_extent). Under and beside the roads (keep_cells: the graded grid's own 20 m cells wherever a pavement is within 18 m) the ground is the v0.17.1 graded surface, triangle for triangle, so the seat and the kn5 prep reshape exactly what they always reshaped; past 20 m the kept cells themselves are refined to the 5 m sub-lattice and take the data, feathered by 36 m (keep_cells.refine, applied by the kn5 prep after it has reshaped the near-road ground). Within 250 m of a pavement (and every pocket that encloses) the ground is physical 1GRASS; the rest is the visual-only far ring GRASS_FAR (no physics, no gates, no GrassFX). The band clamp (+-terrain_band_m of the nearest road) holds in full only within clamp_corridor_m of a pavement and releases to the raw DEM by clamp_blend_m: Cowles, the Del Cerro hilltop and the valley walls are 3DEP, uncapped.

ground_release._doc: Ledger 0046 v0.18.0 integration fix round (the truth lens's criterion 4: seven rims within 20 m of a pavement, each on ground criterion 7 held to v0.17.1 and 2-9 m from the real earth). Inside each zone the near-road ground is the bare-earth 3DEP surface (tools/ground_release.py plans a 2 m lattice and reads 3DEP at every node, cached in data/ground_release.samples.json.gz; tools/ground_release_blend.py applies it to TERRAIN in the author stage, after the seat and before the bridge bodies, and puts a concrete rail on the kerb wherever the new ground drops within reach of a car, by drive_test's own excursion rule). A 'bank' zone releases the ground beside the road only (never under the pavement); a 'span' zone also releases it under the deck, never above the deck (min(3DEP, deck - 0.02)). Fix round 2 (2026-10-13, both lenses): no released FACE stands above any pavement anywhere over its area (capped per face, not per vertex: a 2.5 m facet with one corner over the kerb put grass 5 cm through Lake Murray Blvd's lane), and within reach of a pavement the released ground stands no steeper than an earth batter of 1.5 m per metre from the pavement's edge, up (a cut) or down (a fill, only beside pavement that sits on the ground), so a built sidewalk wider than the real one meets the creek bank as a steep bank, not a 3-4 m vertical curtain; the old 'never above the nearest pavement' cap is gone (it pinned the real 3.6 m terrace between Alvarado and College's south approach down to Alvarado's height). Fix round 2 adds four zones: college_i8_span and lmb_i8_span (each overcrossing's whole real span: the I-8 had climbed the ground the draft seated at the decks) and alvarado_college_terrace and college_approach_foot (the real terrace between Alvarado and College's south approach, which the build held at Alvarado's height out to 16 m and met the released terrace in a 3-4 m curtain). Stations s_m are on data/centerline.local.json; sides: left / right of the lap's travel (the street layout's direction); reach_m past the nominal pavement edge (40 m: past the kept cells' refinement band, 20 + 16 m, which the kn5 prep then leaves alone inside a zone, as it leaves its contact feather). Measured 2026-10-13 on fresh 3DEP 1 m: alvarado_creek_bank — Alvarado Creek and its bank drop 2-8 m within 2-20 m of Alvarado Road's south kerb (s 1752-1995), a bank rises 2 m 4-10 m off it (s 1632-1680); college_south_approach — the real road rides an earth embankment at road height to its abutment (s 2586), and the ground under the approach stood 6 m under the road; lmb_alvarado_creek — Lake Murray Blvd crosses Alvarado Creek on a bridge (bare earth 115.8-117.5 m under a 124 m road, s 13435-13457) that the build had filled solid.

grid_grow._doc: Ledger 0054 P0 step 6 (2026-10-14; EXPANSION-PLAN 'grow the 40 m heightfield without moving a single old stake'). Read by scripts-v021 elevation/heightfield.py and tools/grow_heightfield.py (no ship step runs either; the grown grid itself is synced in): the 40 m grid (123 x 93 over the loop's bbox + 150 m) grows by whole cells to 149 x 167 = 24,883 nodes, [32.758650, -117.080708, 32.818620, -117.017103]. Every old node is sampled at its bit-identical position and every consumer projects it where it always did (the grown meta's bbox is the rounded loop bbox shifted by whole cells, written at full precision; 1.4e-14 deg max over all 11,439 old nodes). rows_n = rows_s keeps the meta's mid-latitude (heightfield.py refuses otherwise). Sized by the north route's kept near-road cells (20 m cells within 18 m of a pavement at the aerial's widest per road): 1,617 cells, the furthest 32.8175 N (J4) and -117.0794 W (J3), 119.9 m inside the grown north edge and 120.5 m inside the west one, so no extra rows. Applied in P2 (2026-10-14) together with tier_options.frame.pin rows_n 37 / cols_w 26 and the re-keyed 3DEP cache: data/heightfield.npy + .meta.json are the grown grid (tools/grow_heightfield.py, which runs build_heightfield's own layout and takes every old node from the installed grid, byte for byte; only the 13,444 new nodes came from 3DEP), synced into the workshop by the ship chain. The assembler's scatter and make_treefx's fill number the old cells as before (ledger 0054 P2), so the scenery near the loop does not move.

pin._doc: Ledger 0054 P0 step 6 (2026-10-14); applied in P2 (2026-10-14): rows_n 37 / cols_w 26, in the same change as the grown data/heightfield.npy + .meta.json (tools/grow_heightfield.py: the 11,439 installed nodes byte for byte, 13,444 new ones from 3DEP) and the re-keyed data/terrain.samples.json.gz (tools/remap_sample_cache.py, PASS: source/expansion/p2-proofs/). The lattice frame is computed from THIS anchor - the installed v0.18.0 data/heightfield.meta.json's rounded bbox_swne (40 m grid, 123 x 93) - shifted by rows_n rows north / cols_w columns west of whole 40 m cells, never from a regrown meta's own (re-rounded) anchor, so growing the grid cannot move a lattice node (terrain_tiers.Frame.heightfield; the meta's recorded grid_grow must equal these offsets and its anchor must be this one shifted, else ValueError). Offsets 0 on the installed meta = today's frame, bit for bit. P2 sets rows_n 37 / cols_w 26 in the SAME change that writes the grown heightfield (terrain.grid_grow, scripts-v021 heightfield.py) and the re-keyed 3DEP cache (tools/remap_sample_cache.py --rows-n 37 --cols-w 26: keys shift by [+416, -592] base units, the identity proof is the tool's).

planned_pavement._doc: Ledger 0054 P2 (2026-10-14; EXPANSION-PLAN P2 step 1: physical ground within 250 m of every new pavement, the enclosed pocket included, before the roads exist). The north network's authored intermediate (tools/author_expansion.py: the four pieces at their stations with the wider curb offset as half-width, the J2-J4 pad outlines, the six see-only stubs) marks the TIERS and the PHYSICAL ground exactly as a built pavement does (terrain_tiers.Topology plan_lines; terrain_sample.planned_inputs), so the ground over the expansion is planned, sampled from 3DEP and tiled now. It never marks keep_cells / refine and is never pavement for the break lines, the clamp or the feather: those follow the BUILT roads, which P3 adds (route_connectors takes the pieces; then this key is retired). The plan is stale when the intermediate changes (inputs_md5).

tier_options._doc: frame: the lattice is anchored on data/heightfield.meta.json upsampled x2 (the assembler's graded 20 m grid; ~20.07 x 19.98 m at Lake Murray), so cell_m 40 / 20 / 5 are 2, 1 and 1/4 of its cells. keep_cells: every grid cell within 18 m of a pavement keeps its own two triangles and graded heights (the seat moves ground <= 11.1 m past a connector's pavement and subdivides <= 15.1 m; the prep pins <= 9 m and subdivides <= 16 m of a road vertex), so near-road ground and every near-road gate are exactly v0.17.1's. x_split: a centre vertex, longest edge = the cell side (5.0 m, 20.1 m) — criterion 5's 7 m / 28.3 m. physical_within_m: the 1GRASS extent (drive_test sweeps <= 20 m off the road; TreeFX fills <= 200 m). keep_surface_m / keep_feather_m: the graded surface is kept to 20 m (the conform corridor) and feathered into the data over 16 m (the conform blend), by pavement distance. keep_cells.refine (ledger 0046 fix round, 2026-10-12): a kept 20 m cell reaches ~46 m out, so past the prep's reach it stayed 20 m graded facets (criterion 5) and smoothed the I-8 terrace walls beside Alvarado away; once the seat and the prep have reshaped the near-road ground, the prep (build_kn5_loop._refine_kept_terrain) halves every kept-cell edge over edge_m 5.5 m on faces reaching past move_beyond_m 20 m or centred past min_face_d_m 12 m (coplanar: on the 20 m grid the halving lands on the 5 m x-split sub-lattice), then moves every kept-cell vertex past 20 m onto the 3DEP sub-lattice (planned for every kept cell's 5 m sub-cells not wholly within beyond_m 10 m, sampled like any vertex, under the L3 clamp) feathered exactly as the lattice beside it — one field across the kept edge, so the kept-node feather of 2026-10-12 (which held the kept cells' outer edge on the graded surface) is retired. Within 20 m of a pavement nothing moves (criterion 7). antialias + diagonals (ledger 0046 fix round 2, 2026-10-13): the visual lens's washboard ribs (the concrete Alvarado Creek channel SE of the LMB overcrossing, ~7 m wide and 6 m deep, and a ~3 m ditch on the cut slope west of College) are real 3DEP features narrower than two 5 m cells, point-sampled every 5 m and folded by a fixed diagonal into a staircase. antialias: every 5 m-level vertex (and refine node) takes the tent-filtered 3DEP of the 2.5 m base lattice around it (weights 1/4 1/2 1/4 per axis, terrain_tiers.AA_TAPS) instead of one point — exact on a plane, it only moves vertices where the ground bends inside a cell; in the far ring the move is held to far_max_move_m 0.85 m of the vertex's own 3DEP point (criterion 6's 1 m less a 0.15 m margin, three times the 0.045 m a fresh 3DEP fetch drifts from the cache on steep far slopes: at 0.95 the truth lens read all 106,544 far vertices against fresh 3DEP at max 0.995 m, 152 over 0.95; at 1.0 a re-sample read 3 of 3,000 at 1.003-1.005 m). diagonals: every plain square cell more than beyond_m 20 m from a pavement is split along the diagonal whose corners differ least in height (terrain_tiers.data_diagonals); no vertex moves, kept cells and x-split fans are untouched. Measured by tools/rib_check.py. GATES-CHANGELOG 2026-10-11 / 2026-10-12 / 2026-10-13: 18 / 250 / 20 / 16, 10 / 5.5 / 20 / 12, the tent kernel, far_max_move_m 0.85 and 20 are invented within the ledger's ranges. breaks + keep_batter (ledger 0046 fix round 4, 2026-10-13): the visual lens still saw a washboard west of College — cut-slope benches, risers 4-6 m tall and ~1.5 m wide, running ~8 degrees off the lattice axis: a lattice can only put a riser BETWEEN two rows of nodes, so it sat between rows j and j+1 for ~35 m and then jumped a row (and in the far ring criterion 6 holds the tent to 0.85 m). breaks: on every edge of a plain 5 m cell (no x-split, no hanging node, not kept, all corners more than beyond_m 20 m from a pavement) whose base-lattice midpoint departs from its ends' line by screen_m 0.25 m and which climbs the ground at least as steeply as it crosses it, 3DEP is read every 0.5 m (cached as fine samples); up to max_per_edge 3 points where the lightly smoothed profile departs most from the polyline (tol_m 0.4 m, min_spacing_m 0.75 m) become vertices ON the edge, and the cell is triangulated through them (the least-squares triangulation of its boundary polygon) — the riser runs straight through the cell. corners filtered: the cell corners keep their anti-aliased height. Measured by tools/rib_check.py step_jogs. keep_batter 3.5 / keep_feather_min_m 8: past 20 m the graded surface returns to 3DEP within an earth batter's run of the gap between them (3.5 m per metre, held to 8-16 m; steepest 0.43, never steeper than the 16 m blend where the gap exceeds 4.6 m), so ground 29 m from the LMB approach is the data within criterion 4's 2 m (truth lens s 3800); per node, interpolated by the prep like D and d. All numbers invented, GATES-CHANGELOG 2026-10-13 fix round 4.

corridors._doc: Ledger 0046 E4. Centreline = the median of the two I-8 carriageway chains in airoso data/osm.i8.json (osm_cache is relative to the airoso root; the I-8 ways of data/osm.json plus the 18 ways west of its bbox, fetched from Overpass 2026-10-13 so the corridor reaches the landmark box's west edge: the truth lens's criterion 4 stations at x -4020..-3870 had no 5 m refinement, v0.18.0 integration fix round 2); the corridor is refined to 5 m cells within 80 m of it and every vertex is 3DEP, so the cut walls AND the fills come from the data (raising as well as lowering). The floor every 10 m becomes data/i8.local.json over the whole far box; 2 m cross-sections every 25 m record where 3DEP says the freeway is in cut / on fill. The original 64-point i8.local.json (provenance unrecorded) is kept as i8.legacy.local.json: the legacy trench, guardrails and streetlight skips near the loop were built on it.

road_datum._doc: LAWS L3 'Bridges dip': a deck is held straight between its REAL abutments at the road's REAL height (tools/deck_datum.py, the first draft step: it edits data/centerline.raw.local.json.pre-median in the build project, y only, before median_envelope). Stations are on that pre-median centreline. Abutments measured 2026-10-13 from fresh 3DEP 1 m along the centreline (data/deck_datum.samples.json): College Ave over I-8 rides its south embankment to s 2586 (108.65 m) and its north embankment from s 2683 (~112.5 m); the pre-0046 deck ran 2568-2697 from an approach height read off the slope under the bridge, leaving the road 2.0-3.0 m low for 60 m north of it and a ~10 % climb to catch up (ledger 0046, v0.18.0 integration fix round: criterion 4's section 2050 north rim). Lake Murray Blvd's two decks (over I-8, and over Alvarado Creek just north of 70th St) read 1-2.6 m low (3DEP) and were deferred in ledger 0046 (they run into the lap seam, L13); ledger 0057 declares them here at their real abutments (fresh 3DEP 1 m, 2026-10-14), re-derived inside the 70th / Alvarado profile window, which crosses the seam. PROFILES (ledger 0057, tools/deck_datum.py PROFILE WINDOWS): inside each window the road is fresh 3DEP 1 m at both carriageway centres (mean), every deck span inside held straight, a Gaussian of 3 m, blended over blend_m at each end; the assembler smooths the window with assembler_sigma_y_pts instead of route.smooth_sigma_y_pts. A window whose start is past its end runs through the seam.

profiles.name: college_alvarado_junction
profiles._fold_fan_fit_doc: Ledger 0057 fix round (2026-10-14; replaces round 1's hold_straight_m box). Two gates judge the College/Alvarado hairpin on paths its tight turn bends: verify_fold_fans' pinch paths (the levelled fold fan, rows 763-774, ledger 0050, pinches its inside edge to ONE point; every path inside folds and turns sharply on the corner's medial axis) and drive_test's fixed-offset wheel paths (each metre's sample jumps sideways where the segment normal turns). The junction's real crest fails both (fan DT 0.076-0.087 m; rehearsal 5: street severe 0 -> 10, race 22 / 20 -> 27 / 26). Round 1's box passed by removing the crest: 0.55 m under the real road centre, the stop line's last metres flat. tools/deck_datum.py fold_fan_fit: inside fit_m (pre-median s 2250-2340: the fan's rows, their eased legs and College's last 15 m to the stop line) the profile takes the change with the smallest misfit to the 3DEP target (heights, grades, grade changes) that keeps the fan within dt_max_m 0.05 m (the gate: 0.06) and drive_test's wheel paths there (street, a race lane both ways) at no severe step and no more kinks than v0.18.0 built here - all read on the ribbon the assembler and the weld will build; inside fit_m the 3DEP is read on the plan the assembler builds (its smoothing moves the hairpin's line up to 3.6 m; the junction tilts 8 % across). Solved: fan DT 0.076 -> 0.047 m; wheel paths street 8 kinks / 0 severe (v0.18.0 here: 12 / 0), race 22 / 0 and 20 / 0 (22 / 6, 20 / 6); the built profile within +0.16 / -0.21 m of the target; the crest 111.27 m against a real 111.48 m on the road centre (round 1: 110.93). fit_m stops at 2340: reaching 2360 the fit steepened College's flank into a sag where the seated ground's 10 m facets rose through the road by up to 9 mm (soft tops street 33 -> 39, race 9 -> 21; rehearsal 6). The solve is cached in data/deck_datum.samples.json fold_fan_fits (keyed by everything it reads; a fresh solve reproduces it byte for byte). The road stays a level slab: the race walls' containment band (no_route, verify_fold_fans (7): +-0.28 m about the centre line) cannot hold the junction's 8 % tilt at 14 m from the line.
profiles.why: ledger 0057, Kevin 2026-10-14: 'my cars with clutches would roll back from stoplights there ... Stoplight would be heading onto Alvarado from college'. The junction is a real hump (fresh 3DEP 1 m: crest ~111.8 m at s ~2310; College southbound climbs into it at +5.8 % on both lanes over the last 30 m before the stop line, s 2356 -> 2326 here = local s 2343 -> 2313) that the August heightfield smoothing and the assembler's sigma_y 5 had cut to +3.5 % and 0.8-1.2 m low. From Alvarado's climb to the junction (s 2200) to the bottom of College by the I-8 ramps (s 2530), short of the College deck window (2548)

Alvarado's pitch from the 70th St junction (v0) to s ~112 is real -7.7 % over 100 m (built -6.1 %), and the eastbound wait at 70th faces +8.3 % uphill (built +5.6 %). Through the lap seam (L13): from Lake Murray Blvd north of its I-8 deck (s 13280) over both of its decks (held straight, lmb_over_i8 / lmb_over_alvarado_creek) and the junction to Alvarado at s 230, where the road runs at ~1 % to College

freeway._doc: OFF (Kevin's call, v0.18.0, ledger 0046 'Kevin's decisions'): 0046 decided 'terrain only, NO I-8 pavement ribbon' (Kevin, on the Lariat: extra highways 'look like wavy ribbons'); asked again with a still of the drawn freeway, the stated default stands — OUT for v0.18.0. enabled: false = tools/freeway_i8.py writes no data/freeway_i8.json (and removes a stale one), tools/author_freeway_blend.py never runs, so the I-8 cut is the 3DEP-shaped terrain cut: no slab bed, no batter cut/fill, no held-verge batter. The tool, its tests and its 3DEP cache stay; flipping this to true is the whole switch. History: ledger 0046 v0.18.0 integration fix round (the view lens, twice: from the College Ave and Lake Murray Blvd decks the I-8 cut read as 'a shallow grassy valley ... no freeway'). 0046 left the freeway itself out as Kevin's call (E4: 'a visual-only I-8 pavement ribbon along the floor so more of the corridor reads as a freeway'); this is that ribbon. tools/freeway_i8.py plans both carriageways from the OSM ways the corridor was cut from (data/corridor.i8.json provenance: lanes per way from the OSM lanes tag, 4-6 here; OSM bridge ways left out), tools/author_freeway_blend.py drapes them on the FINAL ground of the prepped scene lift_m above it (no z-fight with the grass, nothing to drive on: no digit prefix, no physics, no gate reads it) with dashed lane lines, edge lines (yellow on the median side) and a concrete median barrier wherever the carriageways run within barrier_gap_max_m. Within the 1ROAD extent the pavement (HIGHWAY_I8_NEAR) and its lines (MARKINGS_I8) are GrassFX occluders so no grass grows through them; beyond it (HIGHWAY_I8_FAR, no lines) it is plain scenery. tools/make_treefx.py keeps every tree off it. lane_m 3.66 (12 ft, the US interstate lane); the shoulders, the lift, the dash and the step are [invented] (GATES-CHANGELOG 0046 v0.18.0 integration).

streetlights._relocate_doc: v0.18.1 integration (2026-10-14): tools/author_lamps_blend.py RELOCATIONS (tools/streetlight_relocate.py) - each entry names ONE post by its base as the draft places it (local x/z, within 1.0 m) and stands it at to_base_xz; seat 'ground' = the draft's rule on the authored ground under the new base (head 8.8 m over it), 'keep' = the draft's head height. The tool exits 1 (loop.blend not saved) if a named post is missing, the new base is on a road, the pole is < 0.5 m from a wall / guardrail, or its foot is not in the earth. Every other lamp stands where the draft put it. Bases are those of the College (0055) lap: its registration shortened the lap 6.565 m and the draft's 55 m spacing re-stations every lamp after College (238 posts, was 239).
streetlights._doc: Ledger 0056 (Kevin 2026-10-14: 'make lighter lamp model' / 'more modern' / 'Taller too'). tools/author_lamps_blend.py stands this model at every post in data/lights.local.json (the post bases do not move). led_cobra = the modern San Diego arterial light from tools/make_streetlight_led.py (CC0): a 35 ft (10.67 m) galvanised tapered steel pole (Caltrans ES-6A Type 21), 12 ft (3.66 m) upswept mast arm, flat-bottom LED cobra head with a twist-lock photocell, flat LED lens at the 38'-9" (11.81 m) ES-6A mounting height (the 2026-10 lamp's light stood 6.94 m over the road), 371 kn5 render points per lamp with its lens (rehearsal, 2026-10-14) against ~4,045. arms 2 = back-to-back heads, the configuration every 2026-10 lamp has (its lamp_post.obj is symmetric); only the road-ward head carries the emissive lens and the CSP light, as before; arms 1 = the single-arm cobra head. ROLLBACK (one key): model 'street_lamp_2026_10' = Kevin's decimated Street_Lamp (assets/models/lamp_post.obj, 11.5 m, 2 cm invisible lens marker) exactly as v0.18.0 shipped it. The light settings in lighting.streetlight are unchanged (see its _doc, 2026-10-14).

ui_description: Lake Murray, San Diego (Kevin's childhood neighbourhood): the real 13.5 km loop of Alvarado Road, College Avenue, Navajo Road, Jackson Drive and Lake Murray Boulevard around the reservoir, from OpenStreetMap at real USGS 3DEP elevation. Three layouts: Lake Murray Free Roam (the open streets) and the Lake Murray Speedway, normal (clockwise) and Reverse (anticlockwise).
_ui_description_doc: Ledger 0047 fix round (2026-10-11): the CM description is per layout (layouts[].ui_description, read first by scripts/ac/track_folder.ui_track_json); this track-level text is the fallback. The old one described the V3 C1 build (split carriageways deleted, 'no phantom opposing lanes') and a Del Cerro sub-loop, even on the race layouts that seal every side street.
_ui_tags_doc: Real public roads: never 'fictional' (the engine default before the 0047 fix round). track_folder prepends 'circuit' on every closed loop — Content Manager refuses Race / Track Day sessions without it, on the street layout as much as the race ones. CM's width is the narrowest declared width of the lap (Alvarado, 13.0 m), measured by track_folder from data/centerline.local.json.
